content: New Dosing Schedule: If you miss a dose of this medication, consult your doctor or pharmacist immediately to establish a new dosing schedule. Storage Instructions: Refer to the product instructions and consult your pharmacist for specific storage details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless explicitly instructed to do so. Dispose of this product properly when it is expired or no longer needed. Last Revision Date: The information provided here was last updated in August 2024. Important Information on Usage: This document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific condition. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete details about this product and your individual health needs. Uses of Meropenem: Meropenem is an antibiotic used to treat a wide range of bacterial infections. It belongs to the carbapenem class of antibiotics. How to Use Meropenem: Before starting treatment, read the Patient Information Leaflet provided by your pharmacist, if available. If you are administering this medication at home, ensure you are thoroughly trained by your healthcare professional on how to prepare and use it. Inspect the medication visually for particles or discoloration before use. Do not use the liquid if either is present. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. For optimal effectiveness, administer this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue using the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Possible Side Effects: Common side effects include swelling, redness, pain, or soreness at the injection site. Other potential side effects include upset stomach, headache, nausea, vomiting, constipation, or diarrhea. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. This is not a comprehensive list of side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Precautions: Before using meropenem, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other carbapenems (e.g., imipenem), penicillins, cephalosporins, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Rarely, this drug may cause headaches, numbness or tingling of the skin, or seizures. Some forms of this medication contain sodium, which may be relevant for individuals on a sodium-restricted diet. Meropenem may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). This medication passes into breast milk. Consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use (including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Notes: While using this medication, your doctor may order lab tests (e.g., complete blood count, kidney function tests) to monitor your condition. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments. Missed Dose: It is crucial to take each dose of this medication as scheduled. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist promptly to determine a new dosing schedule. Storage Instructions (Reiterated): Follow the product instructions and consult your pharmacist for proper storage guidelines. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Discard this product appropriately when it is expired or no longer needed. Final Note: This document is a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete and personalized information regarding this medication and your health needs.
